section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Familiar Vector
section_1.content: Briefly recap the geometric vector we know: arrows in a 2D or 3D coordinate plane. Visualize two arrows (u and v) being added (tip-to-tail) and an arrow being stretched (scalar multiplication). Establish that vectors are usually seen as 'ordered lists of numbers'.
section_1.example: A GPS navigation arrow pointing 'North 5km' and 'East 2km' as a standard coordinate vector.

section_2.title: The Shift: From 'What it is' to 'What it does'
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of abstraction. Explain that a 'Vector Space' is not a collection of arrows, but any set of objects that follow a specific set of rules (axioms). Use an animation of a 'factory machine' where different objects enter, but as long as they interact correctly, the machine works.
section_2.example: Imagine a 'Club' where members don't have to look like arrows; they just have to follow 8 specific club rules (axioms) regarding how they interact with each other and with numbers.

section_3.title: The Core Rules: The Axiom Checklist
section_3.content: Highlight the most critical axioms using icons: Closure (Adding two members stays in the club), Commutativity (Order doesn't matter), and the Identity (The 'Zero' element). Use a graphical split-screen showing these rules applied to arrows on the left and functions on the right.
section_3.example: If you add two 'sad' functions and the result is still a function in your set, you've satisfied the 'Closure' rule.

section_4.title: Case Study: Functions as Vectors
section_4.content: Visualize a sine wave and a cosine wave. Show that you can add them (creating a new wave) and scale them (making the wave taller). Because functions satisfy all 8 axioms, the set of continuous functions is a Vector Space. Use a 'morphing' animation where an arrow slowly transforms into a wave graph.
section_4.example: A synthesizer combining two sound waves (functions) to create a new sound is essentially performing vector addition in a function space.

section_5.title: Visualizing High Dimensions & Subspaces
section_5.content: Introduce the idea that abstract spaces can have infinite dimensions. Use a 'color palette' analogy. Any color can be a 'vector' made of Red, Green, and Blue (basis vectors). Show a 2D plane (subspace) cutting through a 3D space to illustrate where vectors can live.
section_5.example: A digital artist using a 'color picker' device: every color is a vector in the RGB space, and a 'grayscale filter' is a subspace.

section_6.title: Application: Why Abstraction Matters
section_6.content: Explain that by treating things (like images, signals, or signals) as vectors, we can use the same math (Linear Algebra) to solve complex problems like facial recognition or data compression. Show an image being decomposed into a sum of 'basis images'.
section_6.example: A facial recognition robot 'Character' that sees faces not as pictures, but as points (vectors) in a high-dimensional space to find the 'distance' between two people's features.

section_1.content: Briefly recap the geometric vector we know: arrows in a 2D or 3D coordinate plane. Visualize two arrows (u and v) being added (tip-to-tail) and an arrow being stretched (scalar multiplication). Establish that vectors are usually seen as 'ordered lists of numbers'.
section_1.example: A GPS navigation arrow pointing 'North 5km' and 'East 2km' as a standard coordinate vector.

section_2.title: The Shift: From 'What it is' to 'What it does'
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of abstraction. Explain that a 'Vector Space' is not a collection of arrows, but any set of objects that follow a specific set of rules (axioms). Use an animation of a 'factory machine' where different objects enter, but as long as they interact correctly, the machine works.
section_2.example: Imagine a 'Club' where members don't have to look like arrows; they just have to follow 8 specific club rules (axioms) regarding how they interact with each other and with numbers.

section_3.title: The Core Rules: The Axiom Checklist
section_3.content: Highlight the most critical axioms using icons: Closure (Adding two members stays in the club), Commutativity (Order doesn't matter), and the Identity (The 'Zero' element). Use a graphical split-screen showing these rules applied to arrows on the left and functions on the right.
section_3.example: If you add two 'sad' functions and the result is still a function in your set, you've satisfied the 'Closure' rule.

section_4.title: Case Study: Functions as Vectors
section_4.content: Visualize a sine wave and a cosine wave. Show that you can add them (creating a new wave) and scale them (making the wave taller). Because functions satisfy all 8 axioms, the set of continuous functions is a Vector Space. Use a 'morphing' animation where an arrow slowly transforms into a wave graph.
section_4.example: A synthesizer combining two sound waves (functions) to create a new sound is essentially performing vector addition in a function space.

section_5.title: Visualizing High Dimensions & Subspaces
section_5.content: Introduce the idea that abstract spaces can have infinite dimensions. Use a 'color palette' analogy. Any color can be a 'vector' made of Red, Green, and Blue (basis vectors). Show a 2D plane (subspace) cutting through a 3D space to illustrate where vectors can live.
section_5.example: A digital artist using a 'color picker' device: every color is a vector in the RGB space, and a 'grayscale filter' is a subspace.

section_6.title: Application: Why Abstraction Matters
section_6.content: Explain that by treating things (like images, signals, or signals) as vectors, we can use the same math (Linear Algebra) to solve complex problems like facial recognition or data compression. Show an image being decomposed into a sum of 'basis images'.
section_6.example: A facial recognition robot 'Character' that sees faces not as pictures, but as points (vectors) in a high-dimensional space to find the 'distance' between two people's features.

section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Familiar Vector
lecture_lines: We often view vectors as arrows in 2D space.
Adding vectors follows the simple tip-to-tail rule.
Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its length.
animations: Draw a 2D grid with two arrows, u (#0000FF) and v (#FFFF00), starting from the origin.
Move arrow v to the tip of u (tip-to-tail) and draw a resultant arrow u+v (#00FF00).
Stretch arrow u to twice its length to show scalar multiplication, changing its color to #ADD8E6.

section_2.title: The Shift: From 'What it is' to 'What it does'
lecture_lines: Mathematicians define vectors by behavior, not just appearance.
A vector space is any set following eight rules.
If objects follow axioms, they act like vectors.
animations: Display a factory icon (#FFFFFF) in the center with shapes (circle, square, arrow) entering.
Inside the factory, show 'Addition' and 'Scaling' symbols glowing in #FFD700.
Shapes exit the factory; display text 'Follow the Rules' in #FFFFFF above them.

section_3.title: The Core Rules: The Axiom Checklist
lecture_lines: Closure means adding two members stays in the set.
Commutativity ensures the order of addition never matters.
Every vector space must contain a unique zero element.
These rules apply to arrows and functions alike.
Axioms provide a universal language for different objects.
animations: On the left, show two arrows adding up to a new arrow, labeled 'Closure' in #00FF00.
On the right, show two waves adding to a new wave, also labeled 'Closure' in #00FF00.
Show a 'Zero' element icon (#FFFFFF) appearing in both the arrow and wave sections.

section_4.title: Case Study: Functions as Vectors
lecture_lines: Consider functions like sine waves as abstract vectors.
Adding two functions creates a new, combined wave.
Multiplying a function by a scalar changes its amplitude.
Because they follow axioms, functions form a vector space.
This abstraction allows us to treat graphs like arrows.
animations: Draw a sine wave (#FF0000) and a cosine wave (#0000FF) on a shared graph.
Add the waves to create a new combined wave (#800080).
Morph an arrow vector (#00FF00) into the sine wave to illustrate the concept of functions as vectors.

section_5.title: Visualizing High Dimensions & Subspaces
lecture_lines: Vector spaces can have infinite dimensions, like color palettes.
RGB values act as basis vectors for any color.
Subspaces are smaller planes living within larger spaces.
animations: Show three spheres: Red (#FF0000), Green (#00FF00), and Blue (#0000FF) labeled 'Basis'.
Blend them to create a new color point in a 3D coordinate system.
Draw a 3D cube and slice it with a translucent 2D plane (#FFFFFF, 0.3 opacity) labeled 'Subspace'.

section_6.title: Application: Why Abstraction Matters
lecture_lines: Abstraction lets us treat images as high-dimensional points.
Facial recognition calculates distances between these data vectors.
Linear algebra solves complex problems across many fields.
animations: Display a digital face image, then break it down into several 'basis images' in #D3D3D3.
Show a high-dimensional coordinate system with two points representing different faces.
Draw a measuring line (#FFFF00) between the two points, labeled 'Distance'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shifted right to accommodate lecture text
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.9 
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the given title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: The Familiar Vector", 
            [
                "We often view vectors as arrows in 2D space.",
                "Adding vectors follows the simple tip-to-tail rule.",
                "Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its length."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define Colors
        color_u = "#0000FF"
        color_v = "#FFFF00"
        color_uv = "#00FF00"
        color_scaled_u = "#ADD8E6"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_u)

        # Create coordinate system
        # Use a localized NumberPlane within the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        origin = plane.get_origin()

        # Define vectors relative to plane coordinates
        vec_u_coords = [1, 2, 0]
        vec_v_coords = [2, -1, 0]

        arrow_u = Arrow(
            start=origin, 
            end=plane.c2p(*vec_u_coords), 
            buff=0, 
            color=color_u, 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_u = MathTex(r"\vec{u}", color=color_u, font_size=24)
        label_u.next_to(arrow_u.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        arrow_v = Arrow(
            start=origin, 
            end=plane.c2p(*vec_v_coords), 
            buff=0, 
            color=color_v, 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_v = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=color_v, font_size=24)
        label_v.next_to(arrow_v.get_end(), DR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_u), Write(label_u), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_v), Write(label_v), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Revert previous highlight, highlight current
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_uv)

        # Tip-to-tail rule
        # Move arrow_v to end of arrow_u
        new_v_start = arrow_u.get_end()
        new_v_end = plane.c2p(vec_u_coords[0] + vec_v_coords[0], vec_u_coords[1] + vec_v_coords[1])
        
        # Resultant vector u+v
        arrow_uv = Arrow(
            start=origin, 
            end=new_v_end, 
            buff=0, 
            color=color_uv, 
            stroke_width=8
        )
        label_uv = MathTex(r"\vec{u}+\vec{v}", color=color_uv, font_size=24)
        label_uv.next_to(arrow_uv.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            arrow_v.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(vec_u_coords[0] + vec_v_coords[0]/2, vec_u_coords[1] + vec_v_coords[1]/2)),
            label_v.animate.next_to(new_v_end, DR, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_uv), Write(label_uv), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Revert previous highlight, highlight current
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_scaled_u)

        # Clear v and uv for scalar multiplication demo

            axes.c2p(4, 1, 0),

        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_uv)

        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_scaled_u)

        self.play(FadeOut(arrow_v), FadeOut(label_v), FadeOut(arrow_uv), FadeOut(label_uv))

        scaled_u_coords = [vec_u_coords[0] * 2, vec_u_coords[1] * 2, 0]
        new_end = plane.c2p(*scaled_u_coords)

        label_2u.next_to(new_end, UR, buff=0.1)

        )

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Consider functions like sine waves as abstract vectors.",
            "- Adding two functions creates a new, combined wave.",
            "- Multiplying a function by a scalar changes its amplitude.",
            "- Because they follow axioms, functions form a vector space.",
            "- This abstraction allows us to treat graphs like arrows."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Case Study: Functions as Vectors", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_SINE = "#FF0000"    # Red
        COLOR_COSINE = "#0000FF"  # Blue
        COLOR_SUM = "#800080"     # Purple
        COLOR_ARROW = "#00FF00"   # Green
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"    # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SINE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E6")
        
        sine_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        cosine_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.cos(x), color=COLOR_COSINE)
        
        sine_label = MathTex("f(x) = \\sin(x)", color=COLOR_SINE, font_size=24)
        cosine_label = MathTex("g(x) = \\cos(x)", color=COLOR_COSINE, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sine_label, "B2", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(cosine_label, "B3", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(sine_graph), Write(sine_label))
        self.play(Create(cosine_graph), Write(cosine_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SUM)
        
        sum_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + np.cos(x), color=COLOR_SUM)
        sum_label = MathTex("(f+g)(x)", color=COLOR_SUM, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(sum_graph), Write(sum_label))
        self.play(FadeOut(cosine_graph), FadeOut(cosine_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_SINE)
        
        # Scaling sine graph (Amplitude change)
        scaled_sine = axes.plot(lambda x: 1.5 * np.sin(x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        scaled_label = MathTex("1.5 \\cdot f(x)", color=COLOR_SINE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(scaled_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(sine_graph, scaled_sine),
            ReplacementTransform(sine_label, scaled_label),
            FadeOut(sum_graph),
            FadeOut(sum_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TEXT) # General statement, keep white
        
        axioms_box = VGroup(
            Text("8 Vector Axioms", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text("\u2713 Closure", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
            Text("\u2713 Addition", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
            Text("\u2713 Scaling", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        self.place_at_grid(axioms_box, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        vs_name = Text("Vector Space: C[a,b]", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(vs_name, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(axioms_box))
        self.play(Write(vs_name))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_ARROW)
        
        # Creating an arrow representing a vector
        arrow_vec = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(0, 0, 0),
            end=axes.c2p(1, 1, 0),
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_ARROW,
            stroke_width=8
        )
        
        # Morphing: We'll fade out the axiom text and then morph the arrow into a new sine graph
        self.play(
            FadeOut(axioms_box),
            FadeOut(vs_name),
            FadeOut(scaled_label),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(scaled_sine)
        )
        
        # Final visual: Arrow morphing into sine wave
        final_sine = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x), x_range=[-PI, PI], color=COLOR_SINE)
        self.place_in_area(final_sine, "B2", "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Position arrow at the start of the final_sine's area
        self.place_in_area(arrow_vec, "B2", "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow_vec))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(arrow_vec, final_sine))
        self.wait(2)

        dot1 = Dot(p1_coord, color=COLOR_POINT)

        label2 = Text("Face B", font_size=16).next_to(dot2, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot1, dot2, scale=0.5),
            Write(label1),
            Write(label2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Measuring line and distance label
        dist_line = Line(p1_coord, p2_coord, color=COLOR_DISTANCE, stroke_width=4)
        dist_label = Text("Distance", font_size=20, color=COLOR_DISTANCE).next_to(dist_line.get_center(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(dist_line))
        self.play(Write(dist_label))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

Use an animation of a 'factory machine' where different objects enter, but as long as they interact correctly, the machine works.

        label_u.next_to(arrow_u.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        arrow_v = Arrow(
            start=origin, 
            end=plane.c2p(*vec_v_coords), 
            buff=0, 
            color=color_v, 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_v = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=color_v, font_size=24)
        label_v.next_to(arrow_v.get_end(), DR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_u), Write(label_u), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_v), Write(label_v), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Revert previous highlight, highlight current
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_uv)

        # Tip-to-tail rule
        # Move arrow_v to end of arrow_u
        new_v_start = arrow_u.get_end()
        new_v_end = plane.c2p(vec_u_coords[0] + vec_v_coords[0], vec_u_coords[1] + vec_v_coords[1])

        # Output shapes exit
        circle_out = Circle(radius=0.35, color=BLUE).move_to(target_center)
        square_out = Square(side_length=0.7, color=RED).move_to(target_center)

        self.place_in_area(universal_text, "F1", "F6")
        
        self.play(Write(universal_text))

            Text("\u2713 Addition", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
            Text("\u2713 Scaling", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        self.place_at_grid(axioms_box, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        vs_name = Text("Vector Space: C[a,b]", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(vs_name, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(axioms_box))
        self.play(Write(vs_name))

        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_ARROW)

            end=axes.c2p(1, 1, 0),
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_ARROW,
            stroke_width=8
        )
        
        # Morphing: We'll fade out the axiom text and then morph the arrow into a new sine graph
        self.play(
            FadeOut(axioms_box),
            FadeOut(vs_name),
            FadeOut(scaled_label),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(scaled_sine)
        )
        
        # Final visual: Arrow morphing into sine wave
        final_sine = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x), x_range=[-PI, PI], color=COLOR_SINE)
        self.place_in_area(final_sine, "B2", "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Position arrow at the start of the final_sine's area
        self.place_in_area(arrow_vec, "B2", "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow_vec))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(arrow_vec, final_sine))
        self.wait(2)

        blue_sphere = Dot(color="#0000FF", radius=0.4)
        
        self.place_at_grid(red_sphere, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(green_sphere, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(blue_sphere, "B4")
        
        basis_label = Text("Basis", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_label, "A3")
        
        spheres = VGroup(red_sphere, green_sphere, blue_sphere)
        self.play(FadeIn(spheres), Write(basis_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Blend them to create a new color point in a 3D coordinate system.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a simplified 3D coordinate system (Axes)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"color": BLUE_E},
            tips=True
        )
        # Add a "z-axis" manually for 3D appearance in a 2D scene
        z_axis = Line(axes.c2p(0,0,0), axes.c2p(0,0,0) + np.array([-1, -1, 0]), color=BLUE_E).add_tip()
        coord_sys = VGroup(axes, z_axis)
        self.place_in_area(coord_sys, "C2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Target point: a blended color (e.g., Orange: Red + half Green)
        target_color = "#FFA500"
        blended_point = Dot(color=target_color, radius=0.15)
        blended_point.move_to(axes.c2p(3, 2, 0))
        
        point_label = Text("(R, G, B)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        point_label.next_to(blended_point, UR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(basis_label),
            spheres.animate.scale(0.2).move_to(axes.c2p(0,0,0)),
            FadeIn(coord_sys)
        )
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(spheres, blended_point),
            Write(point_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw a 3D cube and slice it with a translucent 2D plane (#FFFFFF, 0.3 opacity) labeled 'Subspace'.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a wireframe cube
        cube_front = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE_B).move_to(axes.c2p(2,2,0))
        cube_back = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE_B).move_to(axes.c2p(2,2,0) + np.array([-0.5, -0.5, 0]))
        cube_edges = VGroup(
            Line(cube_front.get_corner(UL), cube_back.get_corner(UL), color=BLUE_B),
            Line(cube_front.get_corner(UR), cube_back.get_corner(UR), color=BLUE_B),
            Line(cube_front.get_corner(DL), cube_back.get_corner(DL), color=BLUE_B),
            Line(cube_front.get_corner(DR), cube_back.get_corner(DR), color=BLUE_B)
        )
        cube = VGroup(cube_front, cube_back, cube_edges)
        
        # Subspace plane
        subspace_plane = Polygon(
            axes.c2p(0, 0, 0),
            axes.c2p(4, 1, 0),
            axes.c2p(5, 4, 0),
            axes.c2p(1, 3, 0),
            fill_color=WHITE,
            fill_opacity=0.3,
            stroke_width=1,
            color=WHITE
        )
        
        subspace_text = Text("Subspace", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(subspace_text, "D5")

        self.play(
            FadeOut(blended_point),
            FadeOut(point_label),
            Create(cube)
        )
        self.play(
            FadeIn(subspace_plane),
            Write(subspace_text)
        )
        self.wait(3)

        # Reset colors
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title = "Application: Why Abstraction Matters"
        lines = [
            "Abstraction lets us treat images as high-dimensional points.",
            "Facial recognition calculates distances between these data vectors.",
            "Linear algebra solves complex problems across many fields."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_IMAGE = "#ADD8E6"  # Light blue
        COLOR_BASIS = "#D3D3D3"  # Light grey (from storyboard)
        COLOR_POINT = "#FF69B4"  # Hot pink
        COLOR_DISTANCE = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow (from storyboard)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line: "Abstraction lets us treat images as high-dimensional points."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Digital face image (stylized as a grid)
        face_img = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.2, fill_opacity=0.5, color=COLOR_IMAGE) for _ in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=3, buff=0.05)
        eyes = VGroup(Dot().scale(0.4), Dot().scale(0.4)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15).move_to(face_img[1].get_center() + UP*0.05)
        mouth = Line(LEFT*0.1, RIGHT*0.1, stroke_width=2).move_to(face_img[7].get_center())
        face_compound = VGroup(face_img, eyes, mouth)
        
        self.place_in_area(face_compound, "B3", "C4", scale_factor=1.8)
        self.play(Create(face_compound))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Basis images (smaller grids)
        basis_vgroup = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            b = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.1, fill_opacity=0.3, color=COLOR_BASIS) for _ in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=3, buff=0.02)
            basis_vgroup.add(b)
        
        self.place_at_grid(basis_vgroup[0], "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(basis_vgroup[1], "F4")
        self.place_at_grid(basis_vgroup[2], "F6")
        
        plus1 = Text("+", font_size=20).move_to((self.grid["F2"] + self.grid["F4"])/2)
        plus2 = Text("+", font_size=20).move_to((self.grid["F4"] + self.grid["F6"])/2)
        arrow = Arrow(self.grid["D4"], self.grid["E4"], buff=0.2, color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(
            Create(arrow),
            FadeIn(basis_vgroup, shift=UP),
            Write(plus1),
            Write(plus2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: "Facial recognition calculates distances between these data vectors."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            FadeOut(face_compound, basis_vgroup, plus1, plus2, arrow)
        )
        
        # High-dimensional coordinate system (Axes)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5], y_range=[0, 5], 
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "stroke_width": 2},
            x_length=4, y_length=3
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        p1_coord = axes.c2p(1, 3.5)
        p2_coord = axes.c2p(4, 1.5)
        
        dot1 = Dot(p1_coord, color=COLOR_POINT)
        dot2 = Dot(p2_coord, color=COLOR_POINT)
        label1 = Text("Face A", font_size=16).next_to(dot1, UP, buff=0.1)
        label2 = Text("Face B", font_size=16).next_to(dot2, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot1, dot2, scale=0.5),
            Write(label1),
            Write(label2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: "Linear algebra solves complex problems across many fields."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Measuring line and distance label
        dist_line = Line(p1_coord, p2_coord, color=COLOR_DISTANCE, stroke_width=4)
        dist_label = Text("Distance", font_size=20, color=COLOR_DISTANCE).next_to(dist_line.get_center(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(dist_line))
        self.play(Write(dist_label))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

Demonstrate commutativity by showing u + v being identical to v + u using ghosted arrows.
Display a point at the origin labeled 'Zero Vector' (#FFFFFF) that leaves other vectors unchanged.
Split screen: show arrow addition on left and function addition on right (#FF00FF).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Core Rules: The Axiom Checklist",
            [
                "Closure means adding two members stays in the set.",
                "Commutativity ensures the order of addition never matters.",
                "Every vector space must contain a unique zero element.",
                "These rules apply to arrows and functions alike.",
                "Axioms provide a universal language for different objects."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define colors for each stage
        COLOR_CLOSURE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_COMM = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_APPLY = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_UNIVERSAL = "#FF8000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 (Closure) ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_CLOSURE))
        
        # Arrows (Left side of grid)
        arrow_origin = self.grid["C2"]
        vec_u = Arrow(arrow_origin, self.grid["B1"], buff=0, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        vec_v = Arrow(arrow_origin, self.grid["B3"], buff=0, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        vec_sum = Arrow(arrow_origin, self.grid["A2"], buff=0, color=WHITE)
        label_closure_arrow = Text("CLOSURE", font_size=18, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_closure_arrow, "A1")
        
        # Functions (Right side of grid)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1], y_range=[0, 1], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.0, tips=False).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B4", "C6")
        f_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(PI * x) + 0.2, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        g_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * np.cos(2 * PI * x) + 0.1, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        sum_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(PI * x) + 0.2 * np.cos(2 * PI * x) + 0.3, color=WHITE)
        label_closure_func = Text("CLOSURE", font_size=18, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_closure_func, "A4")

        self.play(Create(vec_u), Create(vec_v), Create(axes), Create(f_graph), Create(g_graph), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Create(vec_sum), Create(sum_graph), Write(label_closure_arrow), Write(label_closure_func), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 (Commutativity) ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_COMM))
        
        comm_arrow = Text("u + v = v + u", font_size=16, color=COLOR_COMM)
        self.place_at_grid(comm_arrow, "D2")
        comm_func = Text("f + g = g + f", font_size=16, color=COLOR_COMM)
        self.place_at_grid(comm_func, "D5")
        
        self.play(Write(comm_arrow), Write(comm_func))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 (Identity) ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO))
        
        zero_dot = Dot(arrow_origin, color=COLOR_ZERO, radius=0.08)
        zero_label_arrow = Text("Zero Vector", font_size=16, color=COLOR_ZERO)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_label_arrow, "E2")
        
        zero_line = axes.plot(lambda x: 0, color=COLOR_ZERO)
        zero_label_func = Text("Zero Function", font_size=16, color=COLOR_ZERO)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_label_func, "E5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(zero_dot), Write(zero_label_arrow), Create(zero_line), Write(zero_label_func))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 (Apply to Both) ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_APPLY))
        
        box_left = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(vec_u, vec_v, vec_sum, label_closure_arrow), color=COLOR_APPLY)
        box_right = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(axes, f_graph, g_graph, sum_graph, label_closure_func), color=COLOR_APPLY)
        
        self.play(Create(box_left), Create(box_right))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 (Universal Language) ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_UNIVERSAL))
        
        universal_text = Text("UNIVERSAL LANGUAGE", font_size=24, color=COLOR_UNIVERSAL)
        self.place_in_area(universal_text, "F1", "F6")
        
        self.play(Write(universal_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout("The Shift: From 'What it is' to 'What it does'", [
            "- Mathematicians define vectors by behavior, not just appearance.",
            "- A vector space is any set following eight rules.",
            "- If objects follow axioms, they act like vectors."
        ])
        
        # Colors for highlights
        H_COLOR = "#FFD700" # Gold color for symbols and rules
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line: Mathematicians define vectors by behavior, not just appearance.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Factory icon creation (#FFFFFF)
        factory_base = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.8, color=WHITE)
        chimney1 = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.7, color=WHITE).next_to(factory_base, UP, buff=0, aligned_edge=LEFT).shift(RIGHT*0.3)
        chimney2 = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.7, color=WHITE).next_to(factory_base, UP, buff=0, aligned_edge=RIGHT).shift(LEFT*0.3)
        factory = VGroup(factory_base, chimney1, chimney2)
        self.place_in_area(factory, 'C3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Input shapes: Circle, Square, Arrow
        circle = Circle(radius=0.35, color=BLUE)
        square = Square(side_length=0.7, color=RED)
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT*0.3, end=RIGHT*0.3, color=GREEN, buff=0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C1')
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'D1')
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'E1')
        
        self.play(
            Create(factory),
            FadeIn(circle, shift=RIGHT),
            FadeIn(square, shift=RIGHT),
            FadeIn(arrow, shift=RIGHT)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Shapes entering factory
        target_center = factory.get_center()
        self.play(
            circle.animate.move_to(target_center).set_opacity(0),
            square.animate.move_to(target_center).set_opacity(0),
            arrow.animate.move_to(target_center).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: A vector space is any set following eight rules.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(H_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Inside symbols glowing in #FFD700
        plus = MathTex("+", color=H_COLOR).scale(1.8)
        dot = MathTex("\\cdot", color=H_COLOR).scale(2.5)
        symbols = VGroup(plus, dot).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6).move_to(target_center)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(symbols))
        self.play(Indicate(symbols, color=H_COLOR, scale_factor=1.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: If objects follow axioms, they act like vectors.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # "Follow the Rules" text above factory
        rules_label = Text("Follow the Rules", font_size=28, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(rules_label, 'B3', 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Output shapes exit
        circle_out = Circle(radius=0.35, color=BLUE).move_to(target_center)
        square_out = Square(side_length=0.7, color=RED).move_to(target_center)
        arrow_out = Arrow(start=LEFT*0.3, end=RIGHT*0.3, color=GREEN, buff=0).move_to(target_center)
        
        self.play(Write(rules_label))
        
        # Exit to right side
        self.play(
            circle_out.animate.move_to(self.grid['C6']),
            square_out.animate.move_to(self.grid['D6']),
            arrow_out.animate.move_to(self.grid['E6']),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Consider functions like sine waves as abstract vectors.",
            "- Adding two functions creates a new, combined wave.",
            "- Multiplying a function by a scalar changes its amplitude.",
            "- Because they follow axioms, functions form a vector space.",
            "- This abstraction allows us to treat graphs like arrows."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Case Study: Functions as Vectors", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_SINE = "#FF0000"    # Red
        COLOR_COSINE = "#0000FF"  # Blue
        COLOR_SUM = "#800080"     # Purple
        COLOR_ARROW = "#00FF00"   # Green
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"    # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SINE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E6")
        
        sine_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        cosine_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.cos(x), color=COLOR_COSINE)
        
        sine_label = MathTex("f(x) = \\sin(x)", color=COLOR_SINE, font_size=24)
        cosine_label = MathTex("g(x) = \\cos(x)", color=COLOR_COSINE, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sine_label, "B2", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(cosine_label, "B3", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(sine_graph), Write(sine_label))
        self.play(Create(cosine_graph), Write(cosine_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SUM)
        
        sum_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + np.cos(x), color=COLOR_SUM)
        sum_label = MathTex("(f+g)(x)", color=COLOR_SUM, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(sum_graph), Write(sum_label))
        self.play(FadeOut(cosine_graph), FadeOut(cosine_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_SINE)
        
        # Scaling sine graph (Amplitude change)
        scaled_sine = axes.plot(lambda x: 1.5 * np.sin(x), color=COLOR_SINE)
        scaled_label = MathTex("1.5 \\cdot f(x)", color=COLOR_SINE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(scaled_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(sine_graph, scaled_sine),
            ReplacementTransform(sine_label, scaled_label),
            FadeOut(sum_graph),
            FadeOut(sum_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TEXT) # General statement, keep white
        
        axioms_box = VGroup(
            Text("8 Vector Axioms", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text("\u2713 Closure", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
            Text("\u2713 Addition", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
            Text("\u2713 Scaling", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        self.place_at_grid(axioms_box, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        vs_name = Text("Vector Space: C[a,b]", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(vs_name, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(axioms_box))
        self.play(Write(vs_name))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_ARROW)
        
        # Creating an arrow representing a vector
        arrow_vec = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(0, 0, 0),
            end=axes.c2p(1, 1, 0),
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_ARROW,
            stroke_width=8
        )
        
        # Morphing: We'll fade out the axiom text and then morph the arrow into a new sine graph
        self.play(
            FadeOut(axioms_box),
            FadeOut(vs_name),
            FadeOut(scaled_label),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(scaled_sine)
        )
        
        # Final visual: Arrow morphing into sine wave
        final_sine = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x), x_range=[-PI, PI], color=COLOR_SINE)
        self.place_in_area(final_sine, "B2", "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Position arrow at the start of the final_sine's area
        self.place_in_area(arrow_vec, "B2", "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow_vec))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(arrow_vec, final_sine))
        self.wait(2)

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the given title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: The Familiar Vector", 
            [
                "We often view vectors as arrows in 2D space.",
                "Adding vectors follows the simple tip-to-tail rule.",
                "Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its length."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define Colors
        color_u = "#0000FF"
        color_v = "#FFFF00"
        color_uv = "#00FF00"
        color_scaled_u = "#ADD8E6"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_u)

        # Create coordinate system
        # Use a localized NumberPlane within the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        origin = plane.get_origin()

        # Define vectors relative to plane coordinates
        vec_u_coords = [1, 2, 0]
        vec_v_coords = [2, -1, 0]

        arrow_u = Arrow(
            start=origin, 
            end=plane.c2p(*vec_u_coords), 
            buff=0, 
            color=color_u, 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_u = MathTex(r"\vec{u}", color=color_u, font_size=24)
        label_u.next_to(arrow_u.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        arrow_v = Arrow(
            start=origin, 
            end=plane.c2p(*vec_v_coords), 
            buff=0, 
            color=color_v, 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_v = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=color_v, font_size=24)
        label_v.next_to(arrow_v.get_end(), DR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_u), Write(label_u), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_v), Write(label_v), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Revert previous highlight, highlight current
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_uv)

        # Tip-to-tail rule
        # Move arrow_v to end of arrow_u
        new_v_start = arrow_u.get_end()
        new_v_end = plane.c2p(vec_u_coords[0] + vec_v_coords[0], vec_u_coords[1] + vec_v_coords[1])
        
        # Resultant vector u+v
        arrow_uv = Arrow(
            start=origin, 
            end=new_v_end, 
            buff=0, 
            color=color_uv, 
            stroke_width=8
        )
        label_uv = MathTex(r"\vec{u}+\vec{v}", color=color_uv, font_size=24)
        label_uv.next_to(arrow_uv.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            arrow_v.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(vec_u_coords[0] + vec_v_coords[0]/2, vec_u_coords[1] + vec_v_coords[1]/2)),
            label_v.animate.next_to(new_v_end, DR, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_uv), Write(label_uv), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Revert previous highlight, highlight current
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_scaled_u)

        # Clear v and uv for scalar multiplication demo
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow_v), FadeOut(label_v), FadeOut(arrow_uv), FadeOut(label_uv))
        
        # Scalar multiplication: 2 * u
        scaled_u_coords = [vec_u_coords[0] * 2, vec_u_coords[1] * 2, 0]
        new_end = plane.c2p(*scaled_u_coords)
        
        label_2u = MathTex(r"2\vec{u}", color=color_scaled_u, font_size=24)
        label_2u.next_to(new_end, UR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            arrow_u.animate.scale(2, about_point=origin).set_color(color_scaled_u),
            Transform(label_u, label_2u),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

                "Every vector space must contain a unique zero element.",
                "These rules apply to arrows and functions alike.",
                "Axioms provide a universal language for different objects."

        vec_sum = Arrow(arrow_origin, self.grid["A2"], buff=0, color=WHITE)

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Core Rules: The Axiom Checklist",
            [
                "Closure means adding two members stays in the set.",
                "Commutativity ensures the order of addition never matters.",
                "Every vector space must contain a unique zero element.",
                "These rules apply to arrows and functions alike.",
                "Axioms provide a universal language for different objects."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define colors for each stage
        COLOR_CLOSURE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_COMM = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_ZERO = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_APPLY = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_UNIVERSAL = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_CLOSURE))
        
        # Arrows (Left side of grid)
        arrow_origin = self.grid["C2"]
        vec_u = Arrow(arrow_origin, self.grid["B1"], buff=0, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        vec_v = Arrow(arrow_origin, self.grid["B3"], buff=0, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        vec_sum = Arrow(arrow_origin, self.grid["A2"], buff=0, color=WHITE)
        label_closure_arrow = Text("CLOSURE", font_size=18, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        self.place_in_area(label_closure_arrow, "A1", "A3")
        
        # Functions (Right side of grid)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1], y_range=[0, 1], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.0, tips=False).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B4", "C6")
        f_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(PI * x) + 0.2, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        g_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * np.cos(2 * PI * x) + 0.1, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        sum_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(PI * x) + 0.2 * np.cos(2 * PI * x) + 0.3, color=WHITE)
        label_closure_func = Text("CLOSURE", font_size=18, color=COLOR_CLOSURE)
        self.place_in_area(label_closure_func, "A4", "A6")

        self.play(Create(vec_u), Create(vec_v), Create(axes), Create(f_graph), Create(g_graph), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Create(vec_sum), Create(sum_graph), Write(label_closure_arrow), Write(label_closure_func), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_COMM))
        
        comm_arrow = Text("u + v = v + u", font_size=16, color=COLOR_COMM)
        self.place_at_grid(comm_arrow, "D2")
        comm_func = Text("f + g = g + f", font_size=16, color=COLOR_COMM)
        self.place_at_grid(comm_func, "D5")
        
        self.play(Write(comm_arrow), Write(comm_func))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ZERO))
        
        zero_dot = Dot(arrow_origin, color=COLOR_ZERO, radius=0.08)
        zero_label_arrow = Text("Zero Vector", font_size=16, color=COLOR_ZERO)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_label_arrow, "E2")
        
        zero_line = axes.plot(lambda x: 0, color=COLOR_ZERO)
        zero_label_func = Text("Zero Function", font_size=16, color=COLOR_ZERO)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_label_func, "E5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(zero_dot), Write(zero_label_arrow), Create(zero_line), Write(zero_label_func))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_APPLY))
        
        box_left = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(vec_u, vec_v, vec_sum, label_closure_arrow), color=COLOR_APPLY)
        box_right = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(axes, f_graph, g_graph, sum_graph, label_closure_func), color=COLOR_APPLY)
        
        self.play(Create(box_left), Create(box_right))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_UNIVERSAL))
        
        universal_text = Text("UNIVERSAL LANGUAGE", font_size=24, color=COLOR_UNIVERSAL)
        self.place_in_area(universal_text, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Load asset
        waves_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/waves.svg"
        wave_l = SVGMobject(waves_path, color=COLOR_UNIVERSAL)
        wave_r = SVGMobject(waves_path, color=COLOR_UNIVERSAL)
        
        self.place_at_grid(wave_l, "F1", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(wave_r, "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(universal_text), FadeIn(wave_l), FadeIn(wave_r))
        self.wait(2)
